problem: Pre-exploration zero-shot VLN methods (e.g. SpatialNav) assume high-quality, human-crafted scene reconstructions (Matterport3D point clouds). A real robot with a monocular RGB camera builds incomplete, noisy, scale-ambiguous reconstructions, and these methods degrade sharply on them.
motivation: A robot in an unseen environment must build its own priors through pre-exploration, and those self-built reconstructions are inevitably noisy. The question is whether a noisy self-reconstructed scene can still reliably guide a zero-shot agent. The authors' observation is that noisy geometry is unreliable as an absolute spatial reference but can still supply verifiable visual evidence.
key_idea: Recover metric scale for monocular SLAM point clouds, then render anticipated future views from the noisy point cloud for each candidate waypoint so the MLLM does counterfactual sub-path selection instead of trusting the map as an absolute reference.
insight: Using the noisy reconstruction as counterfactual visual evidence rather than as a metric map makes the agent robust: on agent-built point clouds SpatialNav loses 13.0 SR on R2R-CE while SpatialAnt loses only 3.0 (Table ablation_pcd). Removing visual anticipation drops SR from 66 to 55 and SPL from 54.4 to 41.4 on the R2R-CE subset. The gains grow with a stronger MLLM backbone (figure only), and a 90° anticipation HFOV is the best trade-off (60° and 120° are worse or similar).
method: Active Scene Discovery: frontier-based DFS exploration with a waypoint predictor builds a grid navigation graph (0.2 m xy, 0.5 m z voxels). Louvain community detection and stair detection partition it into regional subgraphs.

Visibility-aware path planning: per subgraph, hubs are chosen by greedy set cover (coverage threshold τ=0.9, 3 m visibility radius) and ordered by 2-opt TSP with a cost combining path length and a view-overlap penalty. Paths are refined for obstacle clearance, and the robot records RGB video plus IMU traces, doing look-around rotations (±60° horizontal, ±45° vertical) at each node.
Regional reconstruction: SLAM3R reconstructs a local point cloud per video from RGB only (scale-ambiguous).

Cross-modal metric alignment: render depth at the local origin, match the best video frame by SSIM, predict metric depth with Depth-Anything-2, and set the scale factor as the mean ratio of metric to rendered depth over valid pixels.
Global pose integration: rotate and translate each metric-scaled regional cloud into a global frame using the path start pose and matched-frame heading, then merge all clouds.

Visual anticipation: for each candidate waypoint, render a 256x256 future view at the anticipated heading via Gaussian-splatting-style projection (3x3 Gaussian kernel, depth-tolerance occlusion handling), with a default 90° HFOV.

Counterfactual sub-path selection: GPT-5.1 receives the instruction, compressed visual history, each candidate as observed view + action + anticipated view, and a top-down occupancy spatial map. It selects the sub-path that best matches the instruction.

setting.observation: monocular RGB panorama (12 views at 30° intervals), IMU traces; metric depth for waypoint predictor from simulator (sim) or Depth-Anything-2 (real); pre-explored reconstructed point cloud
setting.action_space: continuous local waypoints from a waypoint predictor plus a backtrack action
setting.simulator: Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE) plus real world (Hello Robot)
setting.privileged: pre-exploration of the test scene (agent-reconstructed point cloud); simulator-rendered metric depth for the waypoint predictor in sim; human-curated Matterport3D point clouds only in the H ablation

numbers_note: The MLLM backbone comparison is given only as a figure with no numbers. The R2R-CE and RxR-CE results are on random subsets of val-unseen (100 and 195 episodes). The HFOV ablation rows (60°, 120°) were not included as separate entries.
results: SpatialAnt reaches 66.0 SR on R2R-CE, above SpatialNav's 64.0 and marginally above supervised Efficient-VLN's 64.2. On RxR-CE it reaches 50.8 SR, versus 32.4 for the strongest zero-shot baseline, SpatialNav. On a real Hello Robot it reaches 52% SR against 32% for SmartWay and 20% for VLN-BERT.
limitations: Evaluation uses small random subsets (100 and 195 episodes; 25 real-world paths), so variance is high. Simulation still relies on simulator-rendered depth for the waypoint predictor.
Requires an expensive pre-exploration phase (about 10 min per region, plus around 200 s of reconstruction) and a closed-source GPT-5.1 policy; the agent-built map is static.
The anticipation quality depends on the waypoint predictor's candidates and on point-cloud holes; a wider HFOV (120°) degrades results.
